title: Mahila Congress holds protest in Thiruvananthapuram demanding CEC resignation

tea.why: Protesters oppose the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging mass deletion of voters' names.
tea.want: The resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the withdrawal of the electoral roll revision process.
tea.changed: Nov 21: The Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress held a protest outside the Lok Bhavan in Thiruvananthapuram.

summary: The Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress organised a protest titled 'Kerala Jantar Mantar' outside the Lok Bhavan in Thiruvananthapuram on November 21, 2026. The demonstration, which featured a public trial of an effigy representing Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, was held to demand his resignation. Organisers and speakers, including AICC general secretary Deepa Dasmunsi, alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls led to the deletion of millions of names across India. Participants, including various Congress party leaders and members of the United Democratic Front, pledged to continue their agitation until their demands are met. The event was described by organisers as part of a broader effort to protect the Constitution and democratic systems in India. No official response from the Election Commission was reported in the provided sources.
demands: Withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Mahila Congress staged a protest outside the Lok Bhavan in Thiruvananthapuram to demand the resignation of the CEC.
